units: pixels and seconds; no metric scale anywhere in this record
description: Camera looks straight down at a wooden basketball-court floor. A basketball rolls from the left edge to the right edge along/just below a maroon court line, at nearly constant speed, and leaves the frame. Two shoe toes of the (static) camera operator are at the bottom edge.

objects.name: basketball
objects.identify: the only ball; orange-brown with black seams, ~225 px diameter, rolling left->right
objects.visible_frames: 0-25 (frame 0 partly cut by left edge; 1-21 fully visible; 22-25 increasingly cut by right edge; gone from 26)
objects.reference_point: centre of the fitted (motion-blurred) disk = visible centre
objects.diameter_trend: grows slightly left->right: ~223-225 px at frames 1-12, ~226-231 px at frames 17-23 (ball nearer the camera on the right side, or camera slightly lowered/tilted)
objects.direction: rightwards and slightly up in the image: dy/dx ~ -5/78 px per frame (~ -3.7 deg)

objects.name: maroon_court_line_horizontal
objects.identify: dark maroon painted line crossing the image near y~445-530, rising slightly to the right; the ball rolls along/just below it
objects.frame29_position: top edge y=487 at x=300 -> y=445 at x=1800; bottom edge y=529 at x=300 -> y=489 at x=1800 (slope ~ -0.028)
objects.extent: runs from x~211 (meets left vertical line) to beyond the right image edge

objects.name: maroon_court_line_left_vertical
objects.identify: maroon line going down from the horizontal line at x~211-260 (left side), forms a corner with it
objects.frame29_position: x=217-260 at y=550; x=211-255 at y=750; x=203-230 near y=1050 (partly overexposed by a floor reflection near y~850-950)
objects.length_visible_px: from y~487 (corner) to the bottom edge 1080 = ~590

objects.name: maroon_court_line_right_vertical
objects.identify: maroon line going down from the horizontal line at the right, x~1713-1800

objects.name: blue_stripe
objects.identify: light-blue/white painted stripe, vertical, between the two maroon vertical lines
objects.frame29_position: x=1172-1218 at y=550; x=1194-1241 at y=1050; top end y~507 (touches the maroon line), runs to the bottom edge

objects.name: inner_rectangle_spacing
objects.identify: distance between the two maroon vertical lines

objects.name: operator_shoes
objects.identify: two grey-blue shoe toes at the bottom edge (camera operator); left shoe x~905-1000, right shoe x~1125-1175
objects.frame29_position: left toe top y~1048 (y~1030 in frame 0, due to camera shake); right toe top ~1075, mostly out of frame

objects.name: floor_reflections
objects.identify: bright light reflections on the floor at about (560,855) and (1300,850) in frame 10, and a whitish streak near x~110, y~430-900

objects.name: floorboards
objects.identify: wooden boards running vertically in the image, ~50-100 px wide

events.event: ball already rolling at frame 0, entering from the left edge (centre x~78, partly out of frame)
ball first fully inside the frame
ball crosses the left maroon vertical line (centre x~230)
ball passes over the blue stripe (centre x~1195)
ball crosses the right maroon vertical line (centre x~1740)
last frame with any ball pixels
no bounce, no impact, no direction change; rolling at nearly constant image speed throughout

camera.type: handheld, looking down; small smooth drift, no zoom
camera.shift_definition: cam_dx, cam_dy = image translation of the floor in frame i relative to frame 29 (floor point at (x,y) in frame 29 appears at (x+cam_dx, y+cam_dy) in frame i); phase correlation on floor strips y 0-350 and 650-1000, averaged
camera.note: top and bottom strips differ in dx by up to ~1.5 px (tiny rotation); vertical drift up to ~1.3 px/frame vs ball ~78 px/frame, so camera motion is a <2% effect on the ball's speed

perspective: 2D: top-down view, floor roughly parallel to the image plane. The court lines are slightly non-parallel (left vertical line nearly vertical, right one tilted; spacing between them grows from 1497 px at y=550 to 1560 px at y=1050), so the scale varies by a few % across the image. Ball apparent diameter grows ~3% from left to right.
